questions.shortAnswer: `overwriteSchema` replaces the schema as well as the data. You need it when columns are renamed, dropped, or change type. `mergeSchema` only adds columns.

questions.title: Setting a Table Property
questions.question: Which statement sets a custom property on a Delta table?
questions.shortAnswer: `ALTER TABLE ... SET TBLPROPERTIES` sets key-value table properties. The other options are not valid syntax.

questions.title: Who Reads This Table?
questions.question: A compliance team wants to see which notebooks, jobs, and dashboards read from `gold.revenue_metrics`. Which feature shows this?

choices.D: Unity Catalog lineage on the table's Lineage tab in Catalog Explorer

questions.shortAnswer: Unity Catalog captures lineage at the table level and, where possible, the column level, across queries, notebooks, jobs, dashboards, and pipelines. The Lineage tab lists them, and **See Lineage Graph** shows them as a diagram.
questions.explanation: Lineage shown in Catalog Explorer is kept indefinitely, while the lineage system tables keep a rolling year. Lineage is not preserved when an object is renamed.

questions.title: NULLs in SUM
questions.question: A `revenue` column contains some NULL values. What does `SUM(revenue)` return?

choices.A: NULL, because any NULL makes the aggregate NULL
choices.C: The sum with NULLs counted as 0, and 0 when every value is NULL
choices.D: The sum of the non-NULL values

questions.shortAnswer: Aggregate functions such as `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, `MAX`, and `COUNT(col)` ignore NULLs. `COUNT(*)` counts every row. `SUM` returns NULL only when every value is NULL, which is why option C is wrong.
questions.explanation: If NULL should count as zero, write `SUM(COALESCE(revenue, 0))`.

questions.title: Certifying a Table  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: A data steward wants `main.sales.transactions` to show as certified so analysts know it is the trusted source. What should the steward do?

choices.A: Set the governed tag `system.certification_status` to `certified` on the table, with `SET TAG ON TABLE` or **Assign certification** in the UI
choices.B: Set a table property `certified` to `true` with `ALTER TABLE ... SET TBLPROPERTIES`
choices.C: Grant a `CERTIFY` privilege on the table to the stewards group
choices.D: Add the word "certified" to the table comment

questions.shortAnswer: Certification is the system-governed tag `system.certification_status` with the values `certified` or `deprecated`. In SQL, use `SET TAG ON TABLE` with the tag key quoted in backticks. In the UI, choose **Assign certification** from the object's kebab menu.
questions.explanation: Applying it requires the ASSIGN permission on that governed tag, plus APPLY TAG on the object (or ownership) and USE SCHEMA and USE CATALOG on its parents. A table property or comment does not show the badge (B, D), and `CERTIFY` is not a privilege (C).

questions.title: Finding Certified Data  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: An analyst wants to see only certified tables when searching the workspace. How?

choices.A: Search for `certificationStatus:certified` or use the **Certification status** filter

questions.shortAnswer: Workspace search supports `certificationStatus:certified` and `certificationStatus:deprecated`, and has a **Certification status** filter.
questions.explanation: `SHOW TABLES LIKE` matches table names, not tags (C).

questions.title: Tagging a PII Column  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: An analyst must tag the `ssn` column of `abac.customers.profiles` as PII. Which statement does this?

choices.B: `ALTER TABLE abac.customers.profiles ALTER COLUMN ssn SET TAGS ('pii' = 'ssn')`

questions.shortAnswer: `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET TAGS` adds column tags. In Catalog Explorer, you do the same from the object's Overview page under **Tags** > **Add tags**.
questions.explanation: To tag an object, you must own it or have APPLY TAG on it, plus USE SCHEMA and USE CATALOG on its parents. Tag keys are case-sensitive, and each object can have up to 50 tags.

questions.title: Listing Tagged Columns  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: An analyst wants a SQL list of every column tagged `pii` in a catalog. Where should they look?
questions.shortAnswer: The information schema has views for tags, including `CATALOG_TAGS`, `SCHEMA_TAGS`, `TABLE_TAGS`, `COLUMN_TAGS`, and `VOLUME_TAGS`. Results are limited to objects you have privileges on.

questions.title: Removing Invalid Rows  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: A Delta table `silver.orders` contains rows with negative `amount` values, which are invalid. Which statement removes them?
questions.shortAnswer: `DELETE FROM ... WHERE` removes the matching rows from a Delta table, and the change is recorded in the table history.
questions.explanation: `TRUNCATE TABLE` removes all rows and takes no `WHERE` clause (C). Options A and D are not valid syntax.

questions.title: Filling Missing Values  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: In a cleaned view, a NULL `region` should appear as `'Unknown'`. Which expression does this?
questions.shortAnswer: `COALESCE` returns its first non-NULL argument, so NULL regions become `'Unknown'`. `IFNULL` and `NVL` do the same with two arguments.
questions.explanation: `NULLIF(a, b)` does the opposite: it returns NULL when `a` equals `b` (A).

questions.title: Removing Duplicates  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: `bronze.customers` contains exact duplicate rows. An analyst wants a clean `silver.customers` table with each row once. Which statement does this?

choices.A: `CREATE TABLE silver.customers AS SELECT * FROM bronze.customers GROUP BY ALL HAVING COUNT(*) > 1`
choices.C: `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver.customers AS SELECT DISTINCT * FROM bronze.customers`
choices.D: `CREATE VIEW silver.customers AS SELECT * FROM bronze.customers LIMIT 1`

questions.shortAnswer: `SELECT DISTINCT *` keeps one copy of each identical row, and `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ... AS` stores the result.
questions.explanation: Option A keeps only the rows that were duplicated. Option B is not valid syntax. When rows are duplicates by key rather than identical, use `ROW_NUMBER()` with `QUALIFY ... = 1` instead.

questions.title: Bad Values in a Numeric Column  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: A string column `qty_raw` mostly holds numbers but sometimes holds text such as `'n/a'`. `CAST(qty_raw AS INT)` makes the query fail. What lets the query succeed and turns invalid values into NULL?
questions.shortAnswer: `try_cast` returns NULL when a value cannot be converted, instead of raising an error. You can then handle the NULLs, for example with `COALESCE` or a `WHERE` filter.
questions.explanation: `::` is shorthand for `CAST`, so it fails the same way (B).

questions.title: Three-Level Namespace
questions.question: Which name correctly refers to a table in Unity Catalog?
questions.shortAnswer: Unity Catalog uses a three-level namespace: `catalog.schema.object`, where the object can be a table, view, volume, function, or model. The two-level `schema.table` form comes from the legacy Hive metastore.

questions.title: Granting Read Access
questions.question: Which statement gives the `finance_analysts` group read access to a Unity Catalog table?

choices.A: `GRANT READ ON TABLE main.finance.transactions TO finance_analysts`
choices.B: `GRANT ACCESS ON TABLE main.finance.transactions TO finance_analysts`
choices.C: `GRANT VIEW ON TABLE main.finance.transactions TO finance_analysts`
choices.D: `GRANT SELECT ON TABLE main.finance.transactions TO finance_analysts`

questions.shortAnswer: `SELECT` is the Unity Catalog privilege for reading a table or view. The group also needs `USE CATALOG` on `main` and `USE SCHEMA` on `main.finance`.
questions.explanation: `READ`, `ACCESS`, and `VIEW` are not table privileges. Principal names that contain special characters, such as `@` or `-`, must be quoted with backticks.

questions.title: Removing Access
questions.question: An analyst's access to `finance.transactions` must be removed. Which statement is correct?

choices.A: `DELETE GRANT SELECT ON TABLE finance.transactions FROM contractors`
choices.B: `REVOKE SELECT ON TABLE finance.transactions FROM contractors`
choices.C: `DROP GRANT SELECT ON TABLE finance.transactions FROM contractors`
choices.D: `DENY SELECT ON TABLE finance.transactions TO contractors`

questions.shortAnswer: `REVOKE` removes a privilege that was granted. If the privilege was granted on the parent schema or catalog, revoke it there, because it is inherited.
questions.explanation: `DENY` applies only to the legacy `hive_metastore` catalog and is not supported by Unity Catalog (D).

questions.title: Default Catalog and Schema
questions.question: An analyst runs `USE CATALOG analytics; USE SCHEMA reporting;`. Which table does `SELECT * FROM revenue` read?
questions.shortAnswer: `USE CATALOG` sets the current catalog and `USE SCHEMA` sets the current schema, so unqualified names resolve to `analytics.reporting.revenue`.

questions.title: One Table, Different Rows per User
questions.question: A sales table must show each sales rep only their own region's rows, in every tool and dashboard, without separate tables or views. Which feature does this?

choices.A: A dashboard filter that each user sets
choices.B: A `WHERE` clause written for each user in each query
choices.C: A Unity Catalog row filter on the table

questions.shortAnswer: A row filter is a SQL UDF attached with `ALTER TABLE ... SET ROW FILTER`. Rows where it returns FALSE are excluded at query time, for every query on the table.
questions.explanation: Dashboard filters can be changed by viewers, so they are not security (A). For the same rule across many tables, Databricks recommends ABAC policies based on governed tags.

questions.title: Privileges Needed to Query  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: A group has `SELECT` on `main.sales.orders` but still gets a permission error. Which privileges are most likely missing?
questions.shortAnswer: Reading a table requires `SELECT` on the table plus `USE CATALOG` and `USE SCHEMA` on its parents.
questions.explanation: `MODIFY` is for inserting, updating, and deleting (B). `CREATE TABLE` is for creating tables (C).

questions.title: Granting at the Schema Level  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: A steward runs `GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA main.gold TO bi_readers`. Next week, a new table is created in `main.gold`. Can `bi_readers` read it?

choices.A: No, each new table needs its own grant
choices.B: Only if the new table is external
choices.C: Only after the metastore admin approves it
choices.D: Yes, because privileges granted on a schema apply to all current and future tables and views in it

questions.shortAnswer: Unity Catalog privileges are inherited. A privilege granted on a catalog or schema applies to the matching child objects, including objects created later.
questions.explanation: The group still needs `USE CATALOG` on `main` and `USE SCHEMA` on `main.gold`.

questions.title: Ownership When Someone Leaves  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: An analyst who owns several production tables is leaving the company. What should be done with ownership?

choices.A: Transfer ownership to a group, for example with `ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO data_owners`
choices.B: Nothing, because owners have no special rights

questions.shortAnswer: Every securable object has an owner, and the owner has all privileges on it, including granting privileges to others. Transferring ownership to a group means no single person controls the asset. You can transfer ownership with `ALTER <securable> ... OWNER TO <principal>` or with the **Owner** field in Catalog Explorer.
questions.explanation: The current owner, a metastore admin, the owner of the parent container, or a user with `MANAGE` can transfer ownership.

questions.title: The MANAGE Privilege  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: A team lead must manage who can access a table without becoming its owner. Which privilege allows this?
questions.shortAnswer: `MANAGE` lets a user manage privileges on an object, transfer its ownership, and delete it without being the owner.
questions.explanation: `ALL PRIVILEGES` does not include `MANAGE`. `BROWSE` lets users discover objects and view their metadata without reading data (D).

questions.title: Masking a PII Column  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: HR wants everyone except the `hr_admins` group to see `ssn` as `***-**-****`, in every query on the `employees` table. Which approach fits?

choices.A: Hide the column in a dashboard
choices.C: Store the column in a separate external table
choices.D: Create a SQL UDF that returns the real value only for `hr_admins` members, and attach it with `ALTER TABLE employees ALTER COLUMN ssn SET MASK mask_ssn`

questions.shortAnswer: A column mask is a SQL UDF that returns either the original value or a masked value at query time. Each column can have one mask.
questions.explanation: Hiding a column in one tool does not protect it in other tools (A). Removing `SELECT` blocks the whole table (B).

questions.title: Volume Paths  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: Raw CSV files are stored in a Unity Catalog volume named `landing` in `main.raw`. Which path refers to a file in it?
questions.shortAnswer: Volumes sit at the third level of the namespace (`catalog.schema.volume`), and their files use the path `/Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<volume>/<path>`.
questions.explanation: Reading files requires `READ VOLUME` and writing requires `WRITE VOLUME`, plus `USE CATALOG` and `USE SCHEMA`.

questions.title: Sharing a Saved Query Safely  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: An analyst shares a saved query in a shared folder. Colleagues should be able to run it but not change it. Which permission should they get?
questions.shortAnswer: Workspace objects such as queries, dashboards, notebooks, and folders are secured with access control lists. For queries, the levels are CAN VIEW, CAN RUN, CAN EDIT, and CAN MANAGE. Objects in a folder inherit the folder's permissions.
questions.explanation: Workspace object permissions do not replace Unity Catalog privileges. Running the query still requires access to the tables it reads.

questions.title: Optional Admin Role  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: Which Unity Catalog admin role is optional?
questions.shortAnswer: Account admins and workspace admins are required for every deployment. The metastore admin role is optional, but you need one for some tasks, such as changing the ownership of objects you don't own.
questions.explanation: Databricks recommends assigning the metastore admin role to a group rather than to a single user.

questions.title: Group Checks in a Dynamic View  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: A dynamic view over Unity Catalog data should show salaries only to members of the account-level group `auditors`. Which function should the view use?
questions.shortAnswer: `is_account_group_member()` checks account-level group membership and is recommended for dynamic views over Unity Catalog data.
questions.explanation: `is_member()` checks workspace-level groups only and exists for Hive metastore compatibility, so Databricks advises against it for Unity Catalog (B). Also, do not grant users access to the tables the view reads, or they can bypass it.

questions.title: Uploading a Small File  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: An analyst has a 40 MB CSV file on their laptop and wants it as a table. Which path is quickest?

choices.B: **New** > **Add or upload data** > **Create or modify a table**, then upload the file
choices.C: Ask an admin to create an external location

questions.shortAnswer: The file upload UI creates or overwrites a managed Delta table from small local files. It accepts CSV, TSV, JSON, Avro, Parquet, and text files, up to 10 files at a time with a combined size under 2 GB. It needs a running compute resource and permission to create tables in the target schema.
questions.explanation: Auto Loader and external locations are for files already in cloud storage (A, C). Federation queries external databases (D).

questions.title: Files That Are Not Tables Yet  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: An analyst wants to upload a set of PDF and JSON files so a team can process them later. Where should they go?

choices.A: Into a managed table, using the table upload UI
choices.D: Into a Unity Catalog volume, using **Upload files to a volume**

questions.shortAnswer: Volumes govern files of any format. The UI upload limit is 5 GB per file, and uploading requires `WRITE VOLUME` on the volume. Later, you can select files in the volume and click **Create table** to build a managed table from them.
questions.explanation: The table upload UI accepts only tabular formats (A).

questions.title: Re-running a Load  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: A scheduled `COPY INTO` statement loads files from cloud storage into a Delta table. It runs again before any new files arrive. What happens?

choices.A: Every file is loaded a second time
choices.C: The table is truncated and reloaded
choices.D: Files that were already loaded are skipped, so no duplicates are created

questions.shortAnswer: `COPY INTO` is idempotent. It skips files in the source location that it has already loaded, so it is safe to schedule.
questions.explanation: `COPY_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema' = 'true')` lets the load evolve the table schema.

questions.title: COPY INTO or Auto Loader?  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: A source bucket will receive millions of files over time, and their schema changes often. Which ingestion method does Databricks recommend?
questions.shortAnswer: Databricks suggests `COPY INTO` for files in the thousands and Auto Loader for files in the millions or more. Auto Loader also handles frequently evolving schemas better. `COPY INTO` is easier when you need to reload a subset of re-uploaded files.

questions.title: Auto Loader from SQL  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: A SQL-only analyst wants new JSON files from a volume loaded incrementally into a table every hour. Which statement uses Auto Loader?

choices.A: `CREATE VIEW events AS SELECT * FROM json.'/Volumes/main/raw/events'`
choices.B: `CREATE TABLE events AS SELECT * FROM read_files('/Volumes/main/raw/events')`, re-run each hour
choices.C: `CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE events SCHEDULE EVERY 1 hour AS SELECT * FROM STREAM read_files('/Volumes/main/raw/events', format => 'json')`

questions.shortAnswer: In a streaming table, `STREAM read_files(...)` uses Auto Loader, so each refresh processes only new files. `SCHEDULE EVERY` sets the refresh schedule.
questions.explanation: Re-running a plain CTAS rereads and rewrites everything each time (B). Option D is not valid syntax.

questions.title: Auto Loader Guarantees  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: Why can Auto Loader resume after a failure without loading files twice?

choices.A: It deletes source files after reading them
choices.B: It records discovered files in its checkpoint, which ensures each file is processed exactly once
choices.C: It reloads the whole directory each time and removes duplicates
choices.D: It loads only files whose names contain a date

questions.shortAnswer: Auto Loader (the `cloudFiles` source) stores discovered file metadata in a key-value store in its checkpoint location. That ensures exactly-once processing, and after a failure it resumes from the checkpoint.
questions.explanation: It can also detect schema changes and rescue unexpected data instead of losing it. It never deletes source files (A).

questions.title: Sharing with a Partner That Does Not Use Databricks  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: A company must give a partner live, read-only access to three tables. The partner does not use Databricks. What should the company use?

choices.B: Delta Sharing (now OpenSharing) with the open sharing protocol
choices.C: A weekly CSV export by email

questions.shortAnswer: With OpenSharing (formerly Delta Sharing), a provider shares tables in a read-only share. The Databricks-to-Open protocol serves recipients on any platform, authenticated with bearer tokens or OIDC federation. Data is not replicated, so recipients see updates in near real time.
questions.explanation: Lakehouse Federation is for reading external databases into Databricks, not for sharing out (A).

questions.title: Receiving a Share  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: Another Databricks customer shares tables with your account through Databricks-to-Databricks sharing. How do your analysts start querying them?

choices.A: Run `COPY INTO` from the provider's storage
choices.B: Ask the provider for a JDBC URL
choices.C: A user with `CREATE CATALOG` and `USE PROVIDER` (or a metastore admin) creates a catalog from the share, then grants access to the analysts
choices.D: Upload the provider's files through the UI

questions.shortAnswer: A recipient creates a catalog from the share in Catalog Explorer, with the CLI, or with SQL. Data in a shared catalog is read-only, and you cannot grant write privileges on it.
questions.explanation: Shared data updates in near real time, so no copy or upload is needed (A, D).

questions.title: Pushing Events Through an API  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: An application team wants to push event records from their service straight into a Unity Catalog Delta table over an API, without running a message bus. Which Databricks capability is built for this?
questions.shortAnswer: Zerobus Ingest, part of Lakeflow Connect, is a push-based streaming API that writes records directly into Unity Catalog managed Delta tables. Clients use SDKs over gRPC, a REST API, or other supported protocols.
questions.explanation: The upload UI is for manual files (A), and federation reads external databases (C).

questions.title: Getting Third-Party Data  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: An analyst needs a public weather dataset to enrich sales data, without building an ingestion pipeline. Where should they look first?
questions.shortAnswer: Marketplace lists free and commercial data products from providers. Datasets usually arrive as catalogs of tabular data shared with OpenSharing (formerly Delta Sharing), so there is nothing to copy or schedule.

questions.title: Reading Files from S3 with Governance  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: An analyst wants to load CSV files from `s3://acme-raw/orders/` with `COPY INTO`, governed by Unity Catalog. What must exist first?

choices.A: Nothing, any S3 path can be read by any user
choices.B: A Lakehouse Federation connection to S3
choices.C: A Unity Catalog external location (or an external volume) that covers the path, with privileges granted to the analyst

questions.shortAnswer: Unity Catalog governs access to cloud storage through external locations, which pair a path with a storage credential, and through volumes. `COPY INTO` can load from S3, ADLS, GCS, or Unity Catalog volumes.
questions.explanation: Lakehouse Federation connects to external databases and catalogs, not to raw file paths (B).

questions.title: Star Schema Shape  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: Which description matches a star schema?

choices.A: Every table normalized to third normal form
choices.C: One central fact table with measures, joined to denormalized dimension tables
choices.D: One wide table with every attribute

questions.shortAnswer: A star schema has a central fact table holding measures, such as amounts and quantities, joined to dimension tables such as date, product, and customer. Dimensions are denormalized, with redundant columns, so queries need fewer joins.
questions.explanation: Option B describes Data Vault. Option A describes a 3NF model.

questions.title: Snowflake vs Star  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: How does a snowflake schema differ from a star schema?

choices.A: A snowflake schema has no fact table
choices.B: A snowflake schema stores data only in Snowflake
choices.C: A snowflake schema denormalizes the fact table
choices.D: A snowflake schema normalizes dimensions into several related tables, so queries need more joins

questions.shortAnswer: In a snowflake schema, a dimension such as product is split into product, category, and department tables. That reduces redundancy but adds joins. A star schema keeps each dimension in one denormalized table, which is simpler for BI users.
questions.explanation: The name has nothing to do with the Snowflake product (B).

questions.title: Spotting the Fact Table  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: A model has `dim_customer`, `dim_product`, `dim_date`, and a table with `order_id`, `customer_key`, `product_key`, `date_key`, `quantity`, and `net_amount`. What is that last table?
questions.shortAnswer: It holds numeric measures (`quantity`, `net_amount`) and foreign keys to each dimension, which is what a fact table looks like.

questions.title: Data Vault Building Blocks  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: In a Data Vault model, which table type stores the descriptive attributes of a business entity, and their history?
questions.shortAnswer: Hubs hold the core business entities, keyed by business keys. Links hold only the join keys that relate hubs. Satellites hold the descriptive attributes of a hub or link, with their history.
questions.explanation: Facts belong to dimensional models, not Data Vault (D).

questions.title: Data Vault Keys  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: What does Data Vault modeling recommend as the primary key of a hub, and how can it be built in Databricks SQL?

choices.D: A hash of the business key, built with functions such as `md5` or `sha2`

questions.shortAnswer: Data Vault recommends hashing the business keys to form primary keys. Databricks SQL provides `hash`, `md5`, and SHA functions for this.
questions.explanation: A hash is deterministic, so the same business key always produces the same primary key, load after load. A random UUID changes on every load (C).

questions.title: Models and Medallion Layers  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: According to Databricks guidance, where do Data Vault and Kimball star schemas usually fit in the medallion architecture?

choices.B: Star schemas in silver; Data Vault in gold
choices.D: Data Vault (and 3NF-like models) in silver; Kimball star schemas in gold

questions.shortAnswer: Databricks guidance places Data Vault hubs, links, and satellites, and other 3NF-like models, in the silver layer. Kimball-style star schemas and data marts fit the gold layer, which serves reporting.
questions.explanation: Bronze holds raw, unvalidated data as it arrived (A).

questions.title: What the Gold Layer Is For  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: Which statement best describes the gold layer?

choices.A: Highly refined data, modeled dimensionally with defined measures, that drives dashboards, analytics, ML, and applications
choices.B: Raw files exactly as they arrived
choices.C: A temporary staging area that is deleted daily
choices.D: The layer where schema enforcement is turned off

questions.shortAnswer: Gold holds highly refined views of the data. The medallion docs describe modeling it with a dimensional model, establishing relationships and defining measures. Its users include business analysts, BI developers, data scientists, and executives.
questions.explanation: Raw data is bronze (B). Silver is validated, cleaned, and enriched data.

questions.title: Why Add a Star Schema on Top of a Vault  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: A team loads source data into a Data Vault in silver. Why do they still build star schemas in gold for analysts?

choices.B: Data Vault is write-optimized and needs many joins to answer business questions; star schemas are simpler and faster to query for BI
choices.C: Star schemas cannot be built from a vault
choices.D: Gold must contain exactly one table

questions.shortAnswer: Data Vault is a write-optimized style that adapts well to changing sources. Answering a business question can need many hub, link, and satellite joins. A dimensional model in gold presents the same data in a shape that BI users and tools query easily.
questions.explanation: Satellites keep history, so option A is false.

questions.title: Where Cleaning Happens  *(2025 blueprint)*
questions.question: In the medallion architecture, where are type casting, null handling, and deduplication usually done?
questions.shortAnswer: Silver holds validated, cleaned, and enriched versions of the bronze data. Medallion is a recommended pattern, not a requirement.
questions.explanation: Gold builds business-level models on top of clean silver data (C).
